newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico files new charges against ex-leader's brother.
newsitem.headline: Mexico files new charges against ex-leader's brother.

text.p: Mexican authorities said on Wednesday they have filed fresh money-laundering charges against the jailed brother of ex-President Carlos Salinas.

The Attorney General's Office said in a statement it had pressed charges against Raul Salinas for allegedly laundering some 108 million pesos ($14 million) in ill-gotten gains from January 1991 to April 1992.

Raul Salinas, whose brother governed from 1988-1994, was arrested in early 1995 for plotting the murder of a top politician and has since also been charged with money-laundering and corruption. He has denied all charges.

"The accused, knowing the money was the result of his own illegal enrichment, carried out the operations in order to disguise the origin of the money," the statement, released early on Wednesday, said.
Salinas was cleared of tax evasion charges earlier this year and the government's murder case against him appeared at times to be unravelling, according to experts.
Carlos Salinas himself lives in self-imposed exile in Ireland.
